event_title: Lindsey Graham announces he will seek a fourth term
stated_purpose: seek re-election to the U.S. Senate
observable_function: public announcement by the incumbent
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: opens the cycle the November 2026 ballot is eventually built on
analyst_notes: the incumbent, not the eventual nominee; kept because the vacancy starts here

event_title: Trump endorses Lindsey Graham for re-election
observable_function: endorsement announced; no venue documented
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the endorsement later transfers to his sister, which is why it is logged
analyst_notes: same endorser reappears for Darline Graham in July 2026

event_title: Launches with the 'Unafraid' video
stated_purpose: announce a challenge to Lindsey Graham, framed around RFK Jr.'s HHS confirmation
observable_function: campaign launch video published; a text announcement accompanies it
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: a launch that leads with a clinical/biographical frame rather than a policy list
analyst_notes: video 217 s; venue not applicable (online launch)

event_title: Face the Nation interview on the Senate bid
observable_function: television interview segment, 315 s
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the first sustained national-profile interview of the primary phase

event_title: Campaign event at Greenville Technical College
observable_function: campaign event documented by a Commons photograph description
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the earliest located Andrews appearance in the corpus, and the only one in the Upstate with a named venue
analyst_notes: photograph described as the nominee at a campaign event at Greenville Technical College; no crowd or time recorded

event_title: Wins the Democratic Senate primary with 61.5%
observable_function: primary held; Andrews 226,075 to Brown 110,962 and Freeman 30,374
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: a decisive margin that let the campaign turn to the general early

event_title: Lindsey Graham wins the Republican primary with 56.8%
observable_function: primary held; Lindsey Graham 264,091 of 465,076
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: a 28.9% challenger signals a restless primary electorate that the special primary then re-tests
analyst_notes: the nominee dies 32 days later; the result is superseded, not voided

event_title: Primary-night remarks after winning the nomination
observable_function: speech delivered and posted; 245 s
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: frames the general election while the Republican side still has no nominee

event_title: Death of Senator Lindsey Graham announced
observable_function: death announced; aortic dissection, aged 71
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: converts a routine re-election into a vacancy, an appointment and a three-week special primary
analyst_notes: the structural hinge of the entire race

event_title: Gov. McMaster appoints Darline Graham to the vacant seat
observable_function: appointment announced by the governor; Trump's endorsement follows
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: an appointment that is simultaneously the campaign's launch asset and the central line of attack against her

event_title: Ceremonially sworn in by Chuck Grassley
observable_function: swearing-in ceremony; formal oath administered earlier in the chamber
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: incumbency conferred 112 days before the election

event_title: Announces a campaign for the full six-year term
stated_purpose: seek election in her own right
observable_function: announcement made and covered by CBS
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: separates the appointment from the electoral claim, but only by nine days

event_title: Special-primary filing period opens
observable_function: filing window opened at noon
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: a three-week campaign compressed by statute

event_title: Special Republican primary debate, Gray Media
observable_function: five-candidate debate moderated by Judi Gatson
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the first of two bracketing debates before the 08-11 vote
analyst_notes: participants: Fry, Graham, Lynch, Norman, Sanford

event_title: Special Republican primary debate, Nexstar Media Group
observable_function: five-candidate debate moderated by Alicia Barnes and Carolyn Murray
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: second bracketing debate

event_title: Floor remarks in support of the Russia sanctions bill
stated_purpose: support the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act
observable_function: Senate floor remarks delivered; audio and a still exist on Commons
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the only documented instance of her using the Senate floor as a campaign instrument
analyst_notes: date from the Commons file description; the bill was S.5025, not the enacted H.R. 5334

event_title: Special Republican primary, first round
observable_function: Graham 109,881 (32.8%) and Norman 82,627 (24.6%) advance from ten candidates
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: a plurality, not a majority - the runoff was structurally necessary

event_title: Primary-night speech after advancing to the runoff
observable_function: speech delivered and posted by the campaign; 395 s
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the campaign's own account of the runoff begins here

event_title: Republican runoff debate, SCETV/Newsmax
observable_function: one-hour televised debate between Graham and Norman; moderators Greta Van Susteren, Van Hipp Jr. and Gavin Jackson
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the only head-to-head of the Republican runoff and the source of the competence framing that followed

event_title: Speaks at a Trump rally in Myrtle Beach
observable_function: Graham speaks before Trump at a rally; videos posted 2026-08-21/22
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the endorser becomes a physical surrogate in the runoff's final week
analyst_notes: rally date not established from the retrieved sources; video upload dates only

event_title: Wins the Republican runoff 52.4%-47.6%
observable_function: Graham 193,486 to Norman 175,412
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: an 18,074-vote margin that leaves the losing half of the primary electorate unconsolidated

event_title: Runoff-night remarks
observable_function: remarks delivered; NBC News clip 202 s
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: pivots to the general with the Trump wing intact and the Norman wing not

event_title: Live streaming-newscast interview with WBTV
observable_function: studio interview, 320 s
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the challenger's media strategy runs through local television rather than national studios in this phase

event_title: Kicks off the 'Gas, Grits & Groceries' statewide tour
observable_function: tour kickoff covered by SCETV; 719 s of coverage
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: an economic-message tour launched the week after the Republican runoff settled
analyst_notes: full tour name recovered from a Commons photograph description of a 2026-09-09 stop

event_title: A stop on the Gas, Grits & Groceries Tour
observable_function: tour stop documented by a Commons photograph description
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: confirms the tour ran through early September in unnamed locations
analyst_notes: the description gives the date but not the town

event_title: The only general-election debate, SCETV/SCPR
observable_function: televised debate with Andrews, Graham and Whitener; moderator Gavin Jackson; 3,549 s
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: with one encounter and three candidates, the format constrained any direct two-way exchange
analyst_notes: the only general-election debate in the race

event_title: MS NOW interview on the general-election case
observable_function: interview segment, 380 s
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: national-cable framing of the race as a flip opportunity

event_title: Trump campaigns for her in Clemson
observable_function: the president travels to Clemson to campaign for the appointee
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: an incumbent relying on a surrogate's pull in a college town in the Upstate, three weeks out
analyst_notes: documented through a Commons photograph caption dated 2026-10-21

event_title: Town hall in Fort Mill, York County
observable_function: town hall documented by a Commons photograph description
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the last located campaign event before election day
analyst_notes: York County Democratic Party credited as the photographer

event_title: General election: Andrews 51.14%, Graham 46.64%
observable_function: 2,041,487 votes cast; Andrews 1,044,001 to Graham 952,191
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the first Democratic Senate win in the state since 1998

event_title: Victory speech after the race is projected
observable_function: speech delivered; NBC News 743 s, ABC News 735 s
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: the acceptance frame emphasises healthcare and corruption rather than the seat's national significance
analyst_notes: two independent network uploads of the same remarks

event_title: Concession speech
observable_function: concession delivered; C-SPAN full video 208 s
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: a 112-day incumbency ends with a concession rather than a recount demand
